title: AN OVERVIEW OF DAYLIGHTING SYSTEMS
review_question: To provide an overview and classification of different daylighting systems, illustrating their main principles, characteristics, and abilities to aid in system selection for specific building conditions.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: The review focuses on 'new technologies utilising daylight in buildings' and 'different daylighting systems' available or under development, categorized by their primary function (shading, light guiding, light transport) and light source (diffuse skylight, direct sunlight).

synthesis_conclusions: A wide variety of daylighting systems exist, offering new and optimized ways for daylight utilization in buildings.
Effective daylighting requires careful consideration of the specific system, its adjustment to the building, and matching it to the lighting requirements for its special purpose.
Improper use of daylighting systems can lead to problems such as overheating of rooms or glare, potentially causing system refusal and the implementation of stopgap solutions.
evidence_gaps: There is a need for proper application guidelines and matching daylighting systems to specific building and lighting requirements to avoid negative outcomes like overheating and glare.
limitations: Daylighting systems, if not used correctly or adjusted to building and lighting requirements, can lead to problems such as overheating of rooms or glare.

mechanism_chain.description: Prismatic panels utilize micro-prismatic structures to redirect and diffuse incident sunlight, reducing direct beam intensity and spreading light more uniformly across the visual field, which in turn minimizes high luminance contrasts that cause glare.
